items.question: Why does activity fail to arise once the prior state is destroyed?
premises: A prior state may be destroyed
Activity depends on conditions of that state
Without those conditions activity does not proceed as before
items.inference: As long as the former state is destroyed, activity does not arise in the same way.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the former state is context-dependent
items.plain_english: As long as the former state is destroyed, there is no activity, or it proceeds otherwise.

rows.grounds: compound: destruction is not accepted by you

items.question: Why is darkness not destroyed by light according to the opponent's view?
premises: Light is opposed to darkness
The opponent does not accept destruction of darkness by light
A causal relation of destruction is therefore denied
items.inference: Because you do not accept that darkness is destroyed by light.
uncertainties: The specific opponent addressed is not named in this verse
items.plain_english: Because you do not accept that darkness is destroyed by light.

rows.grounds: abstract reason: capacity to be obstructed

items.question: Why is obstruction fitting for the stable but not for the momentary?
premises: A stable thing can be obstructed
Obstruction requires persistence over time
A momentary thing lacks such persistence
items.inference: Obstruction is fitting for the stable because it can be obstructed, but not for the momentary.
items.plain_english: Because a stable thing can be obstructed, but this is not fitting for a momentary thing.

rows.grounds: compound: in the production of a pot and similar things

items.question: How does a real thing depend on a cause in ordinary production?
premises: Real things are produced in experience
Production of a pot requires causes
Dependence on causes is observed in such cases
items.inference: A real thing depends on a cause, as in the production of a pot and the like.
items.plain_english: A real thing depends on a cause, just as in the production of a pot and so on.

rows.grounds: compound: perishable factors present as causes

items.question: Why do perishable causes fail to operate in the case under discussion?
premises: Ordinary production involves present causes
The case under discussion differs from ordinary production
Perishable causes do not function there
items.inference: In this case, perishable causes, even when present, do not operate at all.
uncertainties: The precise case referred to by 'here' depends on the preceding argument
items.plain_english: But here, perishable causes, even when present, do not operate at all.

rows.grounds: compound: absence of a single uniform nature

items.question: Can a single uniform nature be established through difference or non-difference?
premises: A thing might be considered by difference
A thing might be considered by non-difference
Neither mode yields a single uniform nature
items.inference: Whether by difference or by non-difference, there is no single uniform nature.
items.plain_english: Whether by difference or by non-difference, there is no single uniform nature.

rows.grounds: refers to the previously mentioned nature
compound: will come to be through exclusion
compound: by what means is it established

items.question: How could exclusion itself be established if identity depends on exclusion?
premises: Identity is claimed to arise by exclusion
Exclusion itself requires a basis
No basis for exclusion is provided
items.inference: If that nature is to arise by exclusion, by what is that exclusion itself established?
items.plain_english: If that is to come about by exclusion, then by what is that exclusion itself established?

rows.grounds: compound: exclusion of what is not a pot and so on

items.question: Does excluding non-pots actually allow one to grasp a pot?
premises: Exclusion targets what is not the object
Grasping requires positive apprehension of the object
Excluding non-pots does not by itself present a pot
items.inference: By excluding non-pots and the like, how do you actually grasp a pot?
items.plain_english: By excluding what is not a pot and so on, how do you grasp a pot?

rows.grounds: compound: alternatively at the same time
compound: objects such as pots and others
compound: would reach infinity in the world

items.question: What problem arises if all excluded objects must be grasped simultaneously?
premises: Exclusion of non-pots implies reference to many other objects
Simultaneous grasping would include all such objects
The number of objects in the world is limitless
items.inference: If grasped simultaneously, pot and other objects would lead to an infinite regress in the world.
items.plain_english: Or else, if grasped simultaneously, pots and all other objects in the world would become infinite.

rows.grounds: the property of not being a pot
a common property shared by many

items.question: Can non-potness function as a universal or as a differentiating property?
premises: A universal must be a shared positive property
Non-potness is defined negatively
A non-differentiating property cannot distinguish objects
items.inference: Non-potness is neither a universal nor a differentiating property.
items.plain_english: Is non-potness a universal, or is it not? Indeed, it does not differentiate.

rows.grounds: compound: relation between word and meaning
compound: whose nature is inner manifestation

items.question: What constitutes the real relation between a word and its meaning?
premises: A relation between word and meaning is sought
External exclusion is insufficient
Meaning appears as inner manifestation
items.inference: The expressible relation amounts only to the nature of inner flashing.
items.plain_english: The relation between word and meaning is only this: it has the nature of inner shining.

rows.grounds: compound: from smoke through its relation
when the object is not directly perceived

items.question: Does awareness of fire arise as inner flashing even when fire is unseen?
premises: Smoke is related to fire
Fire may be unseen
Awareness can manifest fire inwardly from smoke
items.inference: From smoke and its relation, does not the flashing of unseen fire occur?
items.plain_english: When fire is unseen, does not its shining arise from smoke through that relation?

rows.grounds: compound: state of being devoid of knowledge

items.question: Why can neither absence of knowledge nor sheer emptiness be established?
premises: Cognition involves inner manifestation
Inner manifestation rules out knowledge-emptiness
Sheer emptiness cannot account for cognition
items.inference: Therefore neither knowledge-emptiness nor sheer emptiness is established.
items.plain_english: Therefore, neither the absence of knowledge nor sheer emptiness is established.

rows.grounds: by means of what is void
act of making known or cognizing

items.question: Why can emptiness neither cognize nor refute anything?
premises: Cognition requires a positive capacity
Refutation requires a positive capacity
Emptiness lacks any such capacity
items.inference: For the empty cannot be awakened by the empty, nor can it be refuted.
items.plain_english: For emptiness cannot be made known by emptiness, nor can it be refuted by it.

rows.grounds: something that must be negated or set aside
compound: if there is no real connection

items.question: How can convention be removed if there is no real connection to ground it?
premises: Convention may need to be removed
Removal would itself rely on convention
Without real connection this becomes problematic
items.inference: If there is no connection, convention would have to be removed only by convention.
items.plain_english: If there is no real connection, then convention would have to be removed only by convention.

rows.grounds: compound: because word and meaning do not truly connect

items.question: In what limited context might exclusion be considered fitting?
premises: Exclusion is problematic as a general theory
Words and meanings may lack direct connection
In that limited sense exclusion might be applied
items.inference: Elsewhere, exclusion may be fitting because of the non-connection of words and meanings.
uncertainties: The scope of 'elsewhere' is not fully specified
items.plain_english: Elsewhere, exclusion may be fitting because words and meanings do not truly connect.

rows.grounds: compound: the example beginning with 'if like leather' and so on
compound: what has been stated by Buddhists
stated or cited as an example

items.question: What Buddhist example is being cited for examination in this argument?
premises: Buddhists have offered illustrative examples
The leather-like example is among them
This example is brought forward for consideration
items.inference: The example beginning with 'if like leather' and so on is what has been declared by the Buddhists.
uncertainties: The full content of the cited Buddhist argument is not given here
items.plain_english: What the Buddhists have declared, beginning with the example 'if like leather' and so on, is cited here.

rows.grounds: compound: those also stated by the Cārvākas

items.question: Do the conceptual objections raised by the Cārvākas succeed in refuting this position?
premises: Cārvākas propose conceptual objections
Such objections are considered here
They do not succeed in refutation
items.inference: Even the conceptual constructions stated by the Cārvākas are not refuting.
uncertainties: The specific Cārvāka arguments are not detailed in this verse
items.plain_english: Even the conceptual objections stated by the Cārvākas do not refute this position.

rows.grounds: compound: because non-being too has the nature of all beings
in the manner of a positive entity

items.question: Why can non-being be treated as having a positive nature?
premises: All beings have their own nature
Non-being is included in consideration
Non-being can be understood in terms of being
items.inference: Because non-being too has the nature of all beings, it is treated as being.
uncertainties: The metaphysical sense of non-being having nature is compressed
items.plain_english: Because non-being too has the nature of all things, it is treated as a kind of being.

rows.grounds: compound: thingness due to having forms like a shard

items.question: How does non-being acquire the status of a thing in experience?
premises: Non-being can appear in concrete forms
Forms like a shard are tangible instances
Such forms confer thingness
items.inference: Because non-being takes forms such as a shard, its thingness is established.
uncertainties: kapāla can mean skull or potsherd; context suggests a concrete remnant
items.plain_english: Because non-being takes forms such as a potsherd, its status as a thing is established.

rows.grounds: in the act of producing or effecting

items.question: Why can non-being not be accomplished as a produced effect?
premises: Production requires positive causal accomplishment
Non-being lacks positive producible nature
Thus its accomplishment as an effect fails
items.inference: Even in the case of non-being, accomplishment through production is not established.
items.plain_english: Even for non-being, accomplishment through production is not established.

rows.grounds: compound: because of pervasion it remains unbroken
the state or nature of Śiva

items.question: Why does the nature of Śiva remain unbroken and all-pervading?
premises: Pervasion implies presence without division
Śiva-ness is characterized by such pervasion
What is all-pervading remains unbroken
items.inference: Because of pervasion, Śiva-ness remains unbroken and all-pervading.
items.plain_english: Because of its pervasion, the nature of Śiva remains unbroken and all-pervading.

rows.grounds: in a philosophical or experiential standpoint
compound: bondage and liberation are declared

items.question: In which philosophical view are bondage and liberation declared within manifoldness?
premises: Some views posit manifoldness
Bondage and liberation are doctrinal categories
These categories are declared within such a view
items.inference: In a view where manifoldness is posited, bondage and liberation are declared.
uncertainties: The specific school is implied rather than named
items.plain_english: In a view where there is manifoldness, bondage and liberation are declared.

rows.grounds: compound: truly stated for one wishing to ascend, for understanding that sequence

items.question: For whom and for what purpose has this teaching been truly stated?
premises: A teaching has been stated
Some aspirants wish to ascend
Understanding the sequence is necessary for them
items.inference: It has been truly stated for one wishing to ascend, for the grasping of that sequence.
uncertainties: The exact sequence referred to depends on the broader context
items.plain_english: This has been truly stated for one who wishes to ascend, so that they may understand that sequence.
